title: Line chart for trends over time
when: Values change over time (daily visits, weight, temperature, balance) and the user wants to see the trend.
prompt:
Goal: A time based SVG line chart with true date spacing, honest gaps, readable axes and a point readout.
Steps:
1. Parse dates to timestamps and sort; x = (t - t0) / (t1 - t0) * plot width, so uneven dates keep real spacing.
2. y domain from min to max padded 5 percent; include zero only when zero matters for the measure.
3. One <path d> per series with M then L commands; start a new M after a missing period instead of bridging it.
4. Ticks: 4 to 7 dates via Intl.DateTimeFormat (day and month, or month and year for long spans) and nice y steps.
5. Label series directly at the line ends and mark the last value with a dot.
6. Readout: on pointermove find the nearest point by binary search, show date and value with a guide line; arrow keys do the same when the svg is focused.
Quality bar:
- stroke-width 2 with vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke.
- At most 4 series.
- Readable at 320 px.
Pitfalls:
- Spacing points by index when dates are uneven.
- Smoothed curves that invent peaks.
- Lines drawn across missing data.
Verify:
- [ ] Points sorted by date.
- [ ] Gaps start new subpaths.
- [ ] svg has role="img" and a title with the trend.
- [ ] Readout works from the keyboard.
Output: js/line-chart.js exporting lineChart(container, series, options) and chart.css.

examples.input: show my weight over the last 6 months as a line
examples.output: lineChart with dated points, monthly ticks, gap for missing weeks, last value labeled
